The closest match is [1], which describes seed-guided clustering that starts from a few user-provided labels and then expands groups by excluding anomalous points. It frames clustering as the dual of anomaly detection and uses an iterative “clustering-by-exclusion” mechanism to isolate fringe points and noise [1].

A second close paper is [7], but it focuses on outlier detection after clustering rather than identifying clusters by starting from a few markers [7]. Papers [4] and [10] also handle robustness and outliers, but they do not describe a seed-guided exclusion-based cluster discovery process [4, 10].
